text.text: In fleeting seconds, Vinicius Junior's redemption spiralled into rage and expletives. He was certain he ended his seven-match goal drought with a delightful strike against Villarreal on Saturday; he celebrated feverishly, manager Jose Mourinho rolled back his vintage with a touchline sprint. But the VAR not only revoked the goal, but also instructed the referee to brandish a straight red card for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair. Vinicius protested, pleaded, cried, and finally staggered to the tunnel. He would miss the El Clasico next week; his shot at revival would drag on. In a tactical sense, Mourinho would heave a sigh of relief, even a feeling of liberation. At the heart of his team’s stuttering start, has been the incompatibility of Vinicius and Kylian Mbappe. Both are indispensable, yet both have struggled to reprise their off-field rapport on the field. The Frenchman, who has carried his World Cup touch into the La Liga with seven goals in eight games, starts functionally as the centre forward, but he invariably veers to the left when Madrid attacks, especially when they are launching a quick counterattack. text.text: Vinicius Jr was not happy with his red card against Villarreal Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr will miss El Clasico against Barcelona after being given a four-game ban. The Brazil international was sent off for pulling Nathan Saliba's hair in Real's 1-0 win against Villarreal last Saturday. His suspension means he will miss games against Sevilla (18 October), Barcelona (25 October), Racing Santander (1 November) and Valencia (7 November). The timing of the decision's announcement angered Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho, as it came hours before his side - featuring Vinicius Jr - faced Roma in the Champions League. "Do you think it's normal that a player from a Spanish team, who has to play a match that is also important for Spanish football, that two hours before the match a player knows he's been given a four-match suspension?" Mourinho said following their astonishing comeback to win 4-3. "Couldn't they do it tomorrow morning? Do we have to come by bus and almost arrive at the stadium when we find out Vinicius has a four-match suspension? "They do things shamelessly now. The cat is out of the bag now. Two hours before the match, a player must know he has a four-match suspension.

"I am deeply honoured to join UNICEF India as a Celebrity Advocate. Growing up playing cricket taught me that every dream begins with an opportunity. Every child and young person deserves the chance to dream big and reach their full potential," Mandhana said. text.text: Red Bull have confirmed that Laurent Mekies will continue his role as Team Principal through 2031. Laurent Mekies has signed a long-term contract extension to remain as Red Bull's CEO and Team Principal, lasting through the 2031 season. The French engineer was promoted from Racing Bulls in July 2025 and led the Milton Keynes-based outfit through a challenging start to this year, which saw them drop behind their rivals under the new regulations. However, their consistent work over the course of 2026 – guided by Mekies – finally paid off as Max Verstappen secured back-to-back victories in Malaysia and Singapore, bringing Red Bull back into contention for regular wins. text.text: Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen have explained what happened at the start of Formula 1’s Singapore Grand Prix, where the Ferrari driver had the best launch but failed to outdo his rival. Despite starting from the dirty side of the track – which admittedly wasn’t as dirty as usual given it had rained the day before – Leclerc had his front axle nearly alongside Verstappen’s within seconds. The four-time world champion, however, drove his opponent towards the inside, to the extent that Leclerc’s front wheels briefly exceeded the white line. The Monegasque braked earlier, and Verstappen was able to retain the lead from the outside. “You don't have much time to think in those moments,” Leclerc said. “I just saw that Max had a bit of a difficult start. I had quite a good start, so I went alongside him. Then there wasn't much space anymore, but I would have done exactly the same. “Then it's quite tricky. I was on the left, a little bit behind him, couldn't see the panels on the right, so you lose a little bit all your references because that's normally on the right that you have your references to brake. text.text: GianPiero Lambiase has served as Max Verstappen's race engineer since 2016 Tom Hart will stand in for GianPiero Lambiase as Max Verstappen 's race engineer at three of the remaining races of the F1 2026 season, PlanetF1.com understands, starting at next weekend's United States Grand Prix. It comes ahead of Hart becoming Verstappen's new full-time race engineer from 2027 as Lambiase prepares to complete his move to McLaren. Lambiase, who has served as Verstappen's race engineer since 2016, announced earlier this year that he will join McLaren as chief racing officer in due course. McLaren commented at the time that Lambiase will start work at Woking 'no later' than 2028. The 2026 season will therefore mark Lambiase's last year as Verstappen's race engineer as he prepares to make the move to his new team. As reported by PlanetF1.com at the time , it emerged in July that Hart will take over from Lambiase on a full-time basis from 2027. The Six Kings Slam has been postponed. Riyadh Season announced on Tuesday that the third edition of its exhibition event, originally scheduled for October 21, 22 and 24, will instead be held from December 27 to 30, 2026. The reason given in the announcement is organizational, though Tennis Majors understands the postponement is linked to the international situation. “The decision reflects Riyadh Season’s commitment to delivering sporting events to the highest standards, following an assessment of the organizational and logistical challenges associated with hosting the tournament and their potential impact on the quality of the audience experience,” the release reads. The Portuguese forward waved a scarf featuring the Saudi flag following Al-Nassr's 3-1 victory over FC Neftchi Fergana in the AFC Champions League Elite, reaffirming his bond with the country and its fans who welcomed him when his career was under scrutiny. There has also been speculation that he could end his playing career in Saudi Arabia. The match was delayed by an hour after an aerial missile alert and explosions were reported across the city. Yemen-based Houthi rebels launched ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh, while Saudi-led coalition forces intercepted and destroyed the incoming projectiles. The fixture went ahead once authorities confirmed the danger had passed. Ronaldo scored Al-Nassr's second goal in the 42nd minute, taking his career tally to 981 goals during the match in Riyadh. text.text: Highlights: Zheng Qinwen beats Mirra Andreeva to become China Open champion Zheng Qinwen became the first Chinese woman to win the China Open by beating Mirra Andreeva in Beijing. Zheng, who entered the tournament as a wildcard ranked number 54 in the world, saved three set points in Sunday's opener before overcoming fourth seed Andreeva 7-5 6-4. The 24-year-old fell to the floor after converting match point and treated the raucous home crowd to some karaoke following her victory speech. "The feeling was incredible. To win here in Beijing in front of my home crowd is one of my dreams," she said. For Zheng, who underwent elbow surgery last year, it was a first WTA 1000 title and her sixth title over all. The triumph brings an end to a two-year title drought for a player who has struggled with form and fitness in the past 12 months. Andreeva, 19, was on top in the early stages of both sets, but was reeled back in both times. The Russian led 2-0 in both sets and 5-4 in the first before Zheng saved three set points and won the remaining 11 points to win the opener 7-5. report.text: Climbing from 19th to ninth on a street circuit sounds like a decent Sunday's work, and for George Russell it was. It also fell short of what Mercedes had pencilled in, and Toto Wolff has now laid out why. Wolff's argument is that Marina Bay punishes anyone who gets close to the car ahead. "I think it's so difficult here to overtake. The moment you catch the car in front, you have such a wake, so much dirty air that you lose downforce, and I think at that stage he was probably one and a half seconds faster than the guys in front of him, but you can't pass. "So our best case scenario was P7. If it would have gone smoothly, I think you know P9 we need to be happy with that. It was a damage limitation race for us with him starting from the back and then so far I think he drove a great race." George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images He also noted, with a bit of dry humour, that the fight through the field "gave them good TV coverage, no?" reports.headline: Warriors blitz Lakers late in NBA Preseason win

report.text: Golden State turned a tight night into a runaway, beating the Los Angeles Lakers 152-114 at Crypto.com Arena in the NBA Preseason . The crowd of 7,471 got a little bit of everything, from hot shooting bursts to a turnover storm late. The Warriors pulled away with a ferocious fourth quarter built on pressure defense and second chances. For full box score details and play-by-play, see the game page on Sofascore . The first quarter offered balance, finishing level at 29-29. By halftime, Golden State had nudged in front 101-88 after a high-paced second period. The Warriors then kept the momentum through the third, taking a 123-101 lead into the final frame. Los Angeles needed a spark, but Golden State instead found another gear. The fourth quarter was all Warriors, 29-13, and the gap ballooned as the minutes ticked down. In short, the night started even, tilted by halftime, and then tipped decisively late. The Warriors’ closing kick separated the teams. Los Angeles could not match the pace or the possession battle over the final 12 minutes. report.text: On a night dominated by the apparent status of Kristaps Porzingis, the absence of the Latvian big was felt at times during the Golden State Warriors’ 101-89 win over the Los Angeles Lakers at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada. Steve Kerr’s intention to spread the floor in a so-called ‘5-out’ alignment banked on players who are able to space to floor — including their center. Porzingis happens to fit that profile, while also being 7-foot-3-inches. Without Porzingis — and also not having Al Horford available tonight — the Warriors were not only small, they were bereft of shooting and spacing personnel. That was apparent at times during this game, where the Warriors were able to rally back from a significant deficit, albeit during a time when both teams’ main characters’ nights were finished (one of them, Luka Doncic, did not suit up for the Lakers). Once again, it was rookie Yaxel Lendeborg who stood out. He finished with 17 points, 5 rebounds, and 4 assists in just under 24 minutes of time on the floor.
